transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sana (Redwood SE), Leo (Redwood SE), Maya (CSM), Ava (HelixStream ML), Derek (Infra), Priya (Product), Samir (SRE), Lina (Security)

Summary: quick gating check, deep-dive on last night's p99 spikes, credential rollout status, and plan for a dedicated-pool stress run.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for carving this out, real quick agenda—ops landing, latency proofing, and security checklist. we'll start with infra status.

[01:05] Derek: yep thanks, we're about 90% through the gateway creds. Samir validated the service account for the Redwood gateway but we hit a NAT throughput limit on staging during the large batch run last night.

[02:10] Samir: yeah the staging NAT saturated around 1.8 Gbps which clipped the tail latency; that's probably why you saw p99 spikes. we have a ticket to push more throughput but wanted to confirm Redwood's expectation for concurrent connections.

[03:12] Sana: ok that makes sense — our runtime does concurrent streams per request, so if the NAT is the bottleneck you'll see token emission delays which show up as p99. On our side we observed bursty long tails when batch size jumped to 8. we suggested batch size 4 for low-latency routes.

[04:30] Ava: can you remind me which tests produced the spike? was that from the canary or long-form generation?

[04:52] Leo: it was the long-form batch test, payload mix B (customer transcripts + summarization). p50 looked fine, p95 was in target, but p99 jumped to around 1.8s extra per token in the worst windows. transcription note: our recorder flagged KV cache as "K-V cash" in last logs so disregard that label in the dashboard.

[06:10] Priya: what's the proposed mitigation? lower batch size, or move to Dedicated? or can caching help?

[06:40] Sana: short term we recommend lowering batch to 4 on the latency-sensitive route and enabling prefix KV caching for repeated context. medium term, Dedicated pool with higher network throughput and pinning a quantized model variant will reduce p99. Dedicated helps because you avoid noisy neighbor egress and can bump up kernel instance counts.

[07:55] Derek: question: the dedicated option — does Redwood require private peering or can we run through the public gateway with static egress? we need to map to our network policy.

[08:18] Jordan: you can do either. Private VPC peering is supported for Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC endpoints; hosted can use our gateway but that uses elastic egress. For compliance you usually want peering and customer-managed KMS.

[09:12] Lina: on the KMS note — we need a checklist for KMS key rotation, HSM support, and proof that keys never leave customer boundary during inference. can you share Redwood's KMS integration doc?

[09:45] Maya: we'll attach the KMS integration checklist and the SOC 2 supplemental doc after this call. Jordan will surface the short form for the security team.

[10:30] Jordan: yes I'll send both. also sending the Dedicated sizing sheet with cost delta and perf numbers.

[11:22] Ava: going back to the p99 spike, did you see any correlation with model quantization settings? we ran quantized floats on staging.

[11:45] Sana: good call — quantization can increase CPU-to-GPU marshalling in some stacks; but our tracing shows GPU compute time was ok, the queuing grew between gateway and runtime when the NAT was saturated. so it's network-first. we still recommend a quick micro-benchmark on quant profiles though.

[13:00] Leo: also note we saw a couple of transient errors labeled "capacity fallback" in the logs — sometimes the system automatically switches to a compatible variant which increases latency. that's a feature but it can show as a spike if the fallback model has slower tokenization.

[14:10] Samir: do you log the fallback event with trace ids so we can correlate?

[14:30] Sana: yes falls are in the trace; we can supply a filter string for the trace UI. we'll also add a custom alert rule to flag fallback occurrences over X per minute.

[15:20] Derek: operationally, what telemetry do we need to capture to show improvement after we bump NAT/peering? request and runtime p99, gateway egress, and token throughput?

[15:45] Jordan: exactly — token/sec, p50/p95/p99, egress bps, and fallback count. Maya: is there a dashboard we can share?

[16:05] Maya: yes we'll drop a per-route dashboard link. note that some fields might be labeled differently in the export (e.g., "model variant" might be shortened to "variant id").

[17:00] Priya: timeline question — if Dedicated is the path we pick, how long to provision and test?

[17:20] Leo: typically 5–7 business days to spin up a dedicated pool and validate network peering, shorter if we reuse an existing region cluster. provisioning includes kernel tuning, quant profile application, and a canary rollout.

[18:05] Ava: cost sensitivity — we need a cost-per-1k-token estimate for both hosted and Dedicated with the quant profile you recommend.

[18:30] Jordan: I'll include that in the spreadsheet; we'll show delta at current projected throughput and at peak 5x. Dedicated tends to win on unit cost when you're at sustained high throughput.

[19:10] Lina: on compliance, what's the retention model for logs? we cannot have raw customer PII in Redwood logs beyond 30 days without a DPA.

[19:40] Maya: you can configure retention limits per account; default is 90 days but we can set it to 30 for the pilot. also we have an option to redact certain fields pre-ingest.

[20:25] Samir: perfect. Derek will coordinate to give us the expected egress profile for the next two weeks so you can size.

[21:05] Derek: I'll put together a small iperf/NAT test and send screenshots. question — will the 2-hour stress test you propose be synthetic only or include replay of production payload?

[21:28] Sana: we'd like a mixed approach: 60% synthetic micro-bench to measure raw token throughput and 40% replay of representative payloads (anonymized). that gives both throughput and tail behavior.

[22:40] Ava: is there any special credentialing needed to run the tests in Dedicated?

[23:00] Jordan: you need the Dedicated service account and the peering set up. we also require a small RBAC role for SRE to view trace IDs. we'll share a checklist.

[24:10] Priya: small question on the fallback policy — can we opt out of automatic fallback to a variant if we prefer to fail instead? we want deterministic failure for now.

[24:35] Leo: yes you can set a strict policy: failover=false and configure a queue depth limit, which will return 429s instead of fallback. we'll document the syntax in the rollout policy config.

[25:50] Lina: on KMS, is it customer-managed key only or can Redwood orbit customer keys via our HSM? we need assurance keys aren't exported.

[26:15] Maya: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via common cloud providers and also HSM-backed solutions for Private deployments. for hosted we can integrate with your KMS through a secure key wrap. the KMS checklist will explain the guarantees.

[27:40] Jordan: ok let's lock the experimental plan: 1) Derek runs NAT throughput tests and shares results by Thursday; 2) Sana runs a 2-hour mixed stress test on Dedicated pool (we'll provision region) — goal to capture p50/p95/p99 and fallback counts; 3) Lina will collect compliance questions and legal reviewer details; 4) Jordan shares pricing and Dedicated sizing.

[29:05] Ava: are there any quick wins for immediate p99 improvement without Dedicated?

[29:20] Sana: yes — reduce batch to 4 on low-latency route, enable prefix caching, and add a rate-limiter in front to smooth bursts. Those three often knock down p99 by 20–40% in staging.

[30:55] Derek: we'll try the batch change tonight and report in the next sync. one more: can Redwood throttle back to single-connection for a subset of traffic?

[31:16] Leo: yes you can apply an API route override to set concurrency=1 for critical routes. there is a small cost in throughput but it helps tail.

[32:40] Priya: ok UX question — how will we be notified if fallback starts occurring frequently? alert channel?

[33:00] Sana: we'll set up an alert rule and webhooks to your PagerDuty; we can also send a Slack daily digest for the pilot.

[34:10] Jordan: let's talk timelines — we should aim to have test artifacts and initial latency run results before next sync. Are we meeting same time next week?

[34:30] Ava: yes same time works.

[35:05] Derek: quick network note — the prod nat is on a different AZ; we'll include that in the screenshots.

[36:20] Maya: Security follow-up: Lina, any blockers you anticipate on getting the SOC supplement?

[36:40] Lina: probably none, but legal needs to triage the DPA changes. I'll ping them and include the legal reviewer in the thread Jordan will create.

[37:10] Jordan: i'll open the email thread and attach the docs after this call.

[38:05] Ava: one more small ask — can Redwood run a tokenization compatibility test on our sample payload? we saw subtle differences in whitespace tokenization that change downstream prompt length.

[38:30] Sana: absolutely, send a few representative snippets and we'll run tokenizer mapping and share token counts and a diff.

[39:20] Priya: perfect. that will help finalize the per-call cost for us.

[40:05] Jordan: ok putting it all together — deliverables and owners: Sana: 2-hour latency run + tokenizer mapping; Jordan: pricing + docs; Derek: network throughput and screenshots; Lina: compliance questions + legal reviewer. We'll reconvene next Tue same time.

[41:40] Ava: thanks everyone, this was helpful.

[42:05] Samir: quick question — is there an ops runbook for failback to hosted if Dedicated provisioning takes longer?

[42:30] Leo: yes we have a rollback playbook and an automated canary that can shift a percentage back to hosted. we'll attach the short playbook.

[43:20] Jordan: great, thanks all. Maya will share decks and the dashboard links.

[44:05] Maya: sending notes and links after the call.

[44:35] Jordan: thanks, see you next week.

[45:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker attribution approximated), auto-captions substituted 'K-V cash' for 'KV cache' in a few spots. Some pauses and interruptions noted as ellipses.
